title: Product PRD: Unified Inference - Overview, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes (2027-03-15)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates the Product Requirements (PRD), high-level design notes, roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and the release notes for the Unified Inference product stream as of 2027-03-15. It is intended for product managers, engineering, go-to-market, sales, and customer success stakeholders.

Summary:
- Product: Unified Inference (hosted API + Dedicated + Private)
- Objective: Provide a single, predictable developer surface for low-latency, cost-efficient LLM inference with tiered deployment modes and clear upgrade/migration paths.
- Target release: phased rollout starting 2027-04 with GA planned for 2027-06.

Key goals (OKRs alignment):
1) Reliability: Meet SLOs for 99.9% availability for Hosted API and 99.95% for Dedicated by GA.
2) Performance: Reduce median text-generation p95 latency by 20% on common 512-token workloads for verified models.
3) Cost controls: Deliver Redwood Optimize integrations that reduce per-token cost by 15% (workload dependent).
4) Enterprise readiness: Complete Private deployment packaging (VPC & on-prem) with KMS integration and compliance artifacts.

Audience and success metrics:
- Primary: Software/ML engineers embedding inference into production services.
- Success metrics: API adoption rate (new API keys using unified routes), cost-per-1k-tokens for typical workloads, number of Dedicated contracts signed, number of Private pilot customers.

Product Requirements (PRD):
1) API & Surface
   - Single REST/SDK surface that supports: text generation, chat, embeddings, classification, reranking, function/tool calling, and structured outputs.
   - Backwards compatibility: Existing Redwood v1 endpoints remain supported for 12 months post-GA with clear migration guides.
   - Streaming: Support chunked streaming responses for generation and chat with reconnect semantics.

2) Model Catalog & Versioning
   - Model metadata: architecture, tokenizer, verified throughput profile, recommended quantization profiles.
   - Pinning: Customers can pin model versions per-route with canary rollout controls.
   - Automatic fallback: Routing policies to fallback to compatible variants (quantized or smaller family) when primary model capacity constrained.

3) Performance & Runtime Controls
   - Batching: Adaptive batching with SLO-aware thresholds.
   - KV/Prefix caching: Transparent prefix cache with configurable TTL per-customer.
   - Quantization profiles: Profiles (FP16, int8, int4) and recommended compute vs quality tradeoffs.

4) Observability & Billing
   - Dashboards: Per-key/token cost breakdown, latency histograms, headroom metrics, error rates.
   - Tracing hooks: Distributed tracing propagation for a request across components.
   - Billing exports: Daily usage CSV & BigQuery export for enterprise customers.

5) Enterprise & Security
   - Private deployment: VPC connector + optional on-prem package; support for AWS/Azure GKE/EKS reference architectures.
   - KMS/HSM integration: Bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flows and audit logging.
   - Compliance: SOC2 and ISO artifacts updated for the unified product surface.

6) UX & Developer Experience
   - Quickstart templates for major frameworks (Node, Python, Java).
   - SDK parity across languages and consistent error models.

Design specs (high-level):
- API design:
  - New top-level path: POST /v2/inference/{route} with body fields: model, input, instructions, functions, stream (boolean).
  - Response envelope includes: request_id, model_version, token_usage, cache_hit (true|false).

- Routing & orchestration:
  - Policy engine evaluates: latency SLO, cost preference, region, customer tier.
  - Route config example (YAML):

    route_name: "chat-consumer-1"
    model: "rw-infer-3b-v1"
    max_latency_ms: 200
    cost_preference: "low"
    fallback_models: ["rw-infer-3b-int8", "rw-infer-1.3b"]

- Observability data model (events emitted):
  - request_received, batch_assigned, model_inference_start, model_inference_end, cache_lookup, response_sent, error.

Roadmap & themes (quarterly priorities):
- Q2 2027: Core GA (API surface, model catalog, adaptive batching, basic observability). Pilot Dedicated baseline customers.
- Q3 2027: Advanced routing policies, Private deployment beta, Redwood Optimize v2 integrations for automated batching/quantization suggestions.
- Q4 2027: Enterprise feature parity (SLA contracts, long-term retention for metrics), pricing packaging launch for Dedicated commitments.

Release and rollout plan (phased):
1) Alpha (internal) - 2027-03-25 to 2027-04-15
   - Internal teams only: integration testing, load tests, perf validation.
2) Closed Beta (selected customers) - 2027-04-16 to 2027-05-31
   - 5-10 pilot customers across startups and mid-market. Dedicated pilot pool opened.
3) Public Beta - 2027-06-01 to 2027-06-30
   - Feature-limited public access; monitor SLOs and iterate on docs.
4) GA - 2027-07-01
   - Official GA with paid tiers, Dedicated contracts, and Private packages available.

Pricing & Packaging notes (guidance for GTM):
- Hosted API (usage-based):
  - Base generation: $0.004 per 1k tokens (small models), $0.016 per 1k tokens (large models).
  - Embeddings: $0.003 per 1k embedding units.
  - Volume tiers: 0-10M tokens standard; discounts apply at >10M tokens (tiered 10-20%, negotiated for >100M).

- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  - Monthly commit model: price per GPU hour + platform fee. Typical bundles:
    - Small (4 GPU): $25k/month + usage; SLA 99.95%
    - Medium (16 GPU): $80k/month + usage; SLA 99.97%
    - Large (64 GPU): enterprise pricing; dedicated account rep.
  - Burst capacity: metered at peak rates; can be included as an uplift.

- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Licensing + support: one-time platform license + annual support fee.
  - Pricing variables: node count, required SLAs, compliance packages.

- Add-ons:
  - Extended observability retention (90/365 days), advanced evals & regression packs, premium SLAs.

- Example pricing scenarios:
  - Startup: Hosted usage 5M tokens/month -> ~$20/month (after free credits) / negotiated discount for early customers.
  - Scale SaaS customer: Dedicated medium bundle + 20M tokens burst -> custom quote with 10% annual commitment discount.

Release notes (2027-03-15 snapshot):
- Features implemented:
  - New /v2/inference API (beta) with streaming & function calling support.
  - Adaptive batching engine v1 integrated into runtime.
  - Model catalog UI: model profiles, verified perf metrics, and quantization recommendations.
  - Basic observability dashboards for latency and token usage per API key.

- Known limitations & mitigations:
  - Private deployment packaging: initial KMS integration is limited to AWS KMS (Azure KMS planned for Q3). Mitigation: documented BYOK workarounds and timeline.
  - Some older SDKs may surface slightly different errors; SDK parity runbook created to coordinate client releases.

Rollout checklist for release engineers & PMs:
1) Confirm infra scale tests passing at 1.5x expected peak QPS.
2) Finalize GA docs and SDK releases (Node/Python/Java).
3) Coordinate price pages and billing surfaces with finance.
4) Prepare migration docs for v1 -> v2 routes and deprecation schedule.
5) Security review complete and compliance artifacts uploaded to security-and-compliance space.

Operational run metrics to monitor post-release:
- API availability (per-region) — target 99.9% Hosted, 99.95% Dedicated
- Error rate (5xx) — target <0.1%
- Median latency (512 tokens) — target p50 <120ms, p95 <400ms for small/medium models
- Cost per 1k tokens (observed vs expected) — alert if >20% delta

Appendix A — Example migration steps (v1 -> v2):
1) Update client SDK to v2.0.0.
2) Change endpoint to /v2/inference/{route}.
3) For streaming: set stream=true and handle chunked events; if previously relying on SSE semantics, follow new reconnect flow.
4) Validate token usage with staging export.
5) Open support ticket for any observed regressions; route to eng-serving-runtime with request_id.

Appendix B — Config table (example route config values):
| field | example | description |
|---|---|---|
| model | rw-infer-3b-v1 | default model for route |
| max_latency_ms | 200 | soft latency SLO (fallback triggered if violated) |
| cost_preference | balanced | balanced |
| cache_ttl_seconds | 86400 | prefix cache TTL |
| autoscale_min_gpus | 1 | minimum GPUs for Dedicated route |
